senses.sense_definition: A compassionate person who generously helps someone in distress.

examples.text: A passing <w>Samaritan</w> stopped to help the elderly driver change a flat tire.
She proved to be a real <w>Samaritan</w> by offering shelter to the stranded tourists.

senses.sense_definition: A native or inhabitant of Samaria, or a member of an ethnoreligious group originating there.

examples.text: The ancient historian described religious interactions between a <w>Samaritan</w> and surrounding communities.
A small population of <w>Samaritans</w> still maintains their historical traditions near Mount Gerizim.

senses.sense_definition: A volunteer who answers calls for the emotional support and suicide prevention charity known as the Samaritans.

examples.text: He spent years training as a <w>Samaritan</w> to support callers dealing with severe emotional crises.
Talking through her troubles with a trained <w>Samaritan</w> provided much-needed comfort during a dark period.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to Samaria or its people and their traditions.

examples.text: Scholars gathered to examine ancient <w>Samaritan</w> manuscripts preserved in the archive.
Archaeologists uncovered artifacts linked to distinct <w>Samaritan</w> cultural practices from that era.

senses.sense_definition: The ancient dialect of Hebrew or Aramaic historically used by the Samaritans.

examples.text: The liturgical text was recorded in <w>Samaritan</w> rather than standard biblical Hebrew.
Linguists compared features of ancient <w>Samaritan</w> with neighboring Semitic languages.
